messages:
support-esc: FYI, enterprise customer (Acotix) just escalated — they saw a sudden billing spike and are asking if their audit logs and stored payloads were impacted during last week's key rotation. They want scope + customer-facing timeline.

jordan: What errors do they report on the API side? Any 5xx/401 spikes in our metrics?

support-esc: They reported a lot of 429 retries then eventual 401s for some requests between 2026-03-05 02:15–02:47 UTC. Billing shows many repeated small requests -> multiplier. They also pinged that some exported audit bundles appear truncated.

maria: Tagging security — I need request ids and sample audit bundle ids. If HSM/KMS rotation affected key access, that could explain 401s.

sasha: I'll pull traces. Initial look at routing — we had a rolling KMS rotation job in that window but it was targeted at a subset of tenant keys (internal note: rotation job id rot-20260305-17). Not supposed to touch customer master keys unless fallback triggered.

incident-bot: New incident created: INC-20260305-1 (severity: P2) — assigned to eng-sre + security.

jordan: Quick repro plan: 1) get request ids from the customer (prefer a few examples). 2) cross-ref with router logs + auth service logs. 3) check HSM audit trail for any failed unwrap operations.

max-prod: Also confirm billing pipeline dedup logic — retries can multiply charge events if dedupe key differs. Did the client SDK change TTL on dedupe key?

kyle-cs: Customer provided sample request ids in email: req_8a3f, req_8a40, req_8a7b. They attached one export file name: audits_20260305_0219.tar.gz which they say is ~1.2MB but used to be ~12MB.

maria: Thanks. I'm pulling HSM logs now. If unwrap failures occurred, HSM audit will show RC errors. Also need KMS rotation timeline: when did rot-20260305-17 start and finish?

sasha: Rotation job start: 2026-03-05T02:10:12Z, finished: 2026-03-05T02:30:05Z for 90% of keys. There was an automated fallback for ~10% of keys that retried and used secondary wrapping key between 02:22–02:45. Those retries could generate 401 for a short window if tokens signed with old key were rejected.

jordan: That lines up with their 02:15–02:47 window. Next: are audit export processes signed/encrypted with the same key material? If so, an interrupted unwrap could produce truncated exports.

maria: Confirmed: export bundles are encrypted server-side with tenant KEKs. If unwrap fails during stream finalize, archive may be incomplete. HSM shows 37 unwrap errors for tenant acotix between 02:23–02:29 (error code HSM-UNWRAP-11).

support-esc: Can we confirm whether their data was exposed or just truncated/failed? Customer is worried about data loss vs exposure.

maria: No evidence of exfiltration. Failed unwrap => archive incomplete, not decrypted to external actor. HSM logs show local failures, no outbound data transfers correlated.

max-prod: Action items for comms: 1) Explain scope (which tenants affected) — looks limited to 12 tenants including Acotix. 2) Explain root cause (rotation fallback produced unwrap failures). 3) Impact: transient auth errors, some exports truncated, billing multiplication from client retries. 4) Remediation and mitigation steps we took. 5) Timeline and ETA for follow-up.

jordan: Remediation steps: a) replay rotation on affected keys with manual validation, b) re-run export finalize for truncated bundles (if blob parts exist), c) trigger billing adjustments for duplicated charges.

sasha: I can re-run finalize on their archive storage job if blob parts exist. Need the bucket path and object prefix from customer. Also recommend we reissue rotation job with stricter backoff and alerting.

kyle-cs: Customer provided s3 path in DM (redacted here). They asked for a timeline for bundle recovery and crediting.

maria: Proposed initial public-facing language (short): "We identified a brief key rotation fallback on 2026-03-05 that caused transient authentication failures for a small number of tenants. This may have resulted in incomplete audit exports and repeated API retries that affected billing. We are: (1) recovering incomplete exports where possible, (2) adjusting billing for duplicate calls, and (3) hardening rotation to prevent recurrence. We will follow up with a full timeline by EOD UTC+0." Thoughts?

support-esc: Good. Customer is asking if this meets audit notification obligations (they are SOC2). Do we need to issue an official security notification or is the standard incident update enough?

maria: For SOC2 customers, we should provide a signed incident summary with scope, root cause, mitigation, and corrective actions. Also include HSM audit extract for their auditors (sanitized). Set as required.

max-prod: ETA: engineering can finish key replay and attempt bundle recovery within 6 hours. Billing team can prepare credits within 8 hours pending verification. Security can produce draft signed summary within 12 hours.

jordan: I'll assign follow-up tasks and update INC-20260305-1. For now, collect: (1) list of affected tenants, (2) sample request ids from customer, (3) bucket/object paths, (4) list of truncated bundles.

kyle-cs: I'll coordinate with the customer on required info and send them the initial template message.

sasha: Starting replay now. Will post status in 30m.

incident-bot: INC-20260305-1 status updated -> investigation in progress.

support-esc: Thanks all. I'll keep customer notified and request permission to share sanitized HSM audit lines for their auditors. :pray:
